clauses.text: **[STU-PRO-167] Slide role folded into Layout.** A slide is an ordinary Folio/StudioLayer frame role in the shared `.handshake` graph, with Layout authoring and Components/Pulse transition bindings; it creates no separate document model. Interop-Fig's pinned `SlideNode` projection has readonly `type = SLIDE`, `clone()`, `getSlideTransition()`, `setSlideTransition(...)` and `isSkippedSlide: boolean`, plus the complete `BaseFrameMixin` transitive capture. Its direct frame fields include nullable readonly `detachedInfo`, `layoutGrids`, `gridStyleId`, `setGridStyleIdAsync(...)`, `clipsContent`, `guides` and nullable `inferredAutoLayout`. The MT MUST consume its applicable thirty-declaration BaseFrame closure from the combined corpus and map each inherited field/method to its existing owner, preserving nullable, optional, mixed and readonly semantics rather than duplicating those engines. In the separately documented source compatibility profile, slides are fixed 1920×1080, direct children of a slide row and not resizable, rotatable or transformable; these are source restrictions, not global restrictions on native Layout frames. Preserve any clone-parent/hierarchy conflict as typed unsupported until an original-runtime fixture resolves it. Author/select/reorder/copy/skip, undo and inspect use the shared command, Controls, Argus and manual surfaces; source-profile incompatibility must be visible.

**[STU-PRO-168] Slide-row role folded into Layout.** A row uses ordered Folio child references and Layout container operations in the same graph. The pinned `SlideRowNode` has readonly `type = SLIDE_ROW`, `clone()` and the complete `OpaqueNodeMixin` plus `ChildrenMixin` surfaces. `ChildrenMixin` has no extends clause; consume its actual captured child/traversal methods and nullable lookup results, not the earlier malformed research metadata. In the source profile, a row is a direct grid child and contains slides only; it is not directly selectable/editable in the source UI. Native authoring may expose row ordering through shared controls, but MUST distinguish that native extension from captured source behavior. Preserve child order, identity and metadata on conversion; a clone-parent conflict requires the same explicit fixture resolution as [STU-PRO-167].

**[STU-PRO-169] Slide-grid role folded into Layout.** The pinned `SlideGridNode` has readonly `type = SLIDE_GRID`, a declared `clone()` and the complete `OpaqueNodeMixin` plus `ChildrenMixin` surfaces. Its source profile permits one top-level grid per source document, rows only, no API creation or direct UI editing, and `clone()` throws; the adapter MUST expose those restrictions as typed capability outcomes and test the negative clone case. This does not prohibit creating or editing native ordered Layout containers in `.handshake`. Map the source grid/row/slide hierarchy onto existing Folio/Layout containers with explicit provenance and stable ordering; frame-grid layout fields are a distinct inherited capability and MUST NOT be conflated with slide-grid hierarchy. Unavailable decoding or source operations are visible limitations, never a substitute document, silent rasterization or parity claim.

**[STU-PRO-170] Interactive-slide role folded into Components.** The pinned `InteractiveSlideElementNode` extends `OpaqueNodeMixin`, has readonly `type = INTERACTIVE_SLIDE_ELEMENT`, `clone()` and readonly `interactiveSlideElementType` with exactly `POLL`, `EMBED`, `FACEPILE`, `ALIGNMENT`, `YOUTUBE`. Components represents the interactive role on an ordinary shared layer; Layout positions it, existing media/embed capabilities supply supported content, and Controls reuses role-specific descriptors on the same assets. The declaration does not specify poll questions/results, facepile participants, alignment rules, embed controls or YouTube payloads. The affected MT's first acceptance criterion MUST recover and pin the complete payload and interaction contract required for working authoring/playback; it MUST NOT invent vendor fields from the role name. Before that proof, preserve unavailable source payloads opaquely within existing bounded import/CKC surfaces and expose a typed limitation, without treating preservation as full parity. No new plugin registry, database, document silo or network entitlement is implied.

**[STU-PRO-171] Slide-transition record folded into Components.** The pinned `SlideTransition` record has exactly the required readonly fields `style`, `duration: number`, `curve` and `timing`; `duration` is explicitly in seconds. Retain the exact source record, numeric presence, token identity and source/version provenance separately from the native transition/easing representation. Its declaration provides no default, hard/soft bounds, precision or step values; [STU-PRO-121]'s 300 ms default and 30 000 ms native bound MUST NOT be applied to this capture. Reject non-finite or unrepresentable values with typed diagnostics and preserve an explicit loss decision, never silently clamp. Components owns the transition description, Pulse owns checked scheduling conversion, and Interop-Fig owns the source mapping. Shared Controls/Argus/manual expose all four fields and mapping outcomes. Source record preservation alone does not prove rendering equivalence.

**[STU-PRO-172] Closed slide-transition style vocabulary.** The source record's `style` is exactly one of these twenty-three tokens: `NONE`, `DISSOLVE`, `SLIDE_FROM_LEFT`, `SLIDE_FROM_RIGHT`, `SLIDE_FROM_BOTTOM`, `SLIDE_FROM_TOP`, `PUSH_FROM_LEFT`, `PUSH_FROM_RIGHT`, `PUSH_FROM_BOTTOM`, `PUSH_FROM_TOP`, `MOVE_FROM_LEFT`, `MOVE_FROM_RIGHT`, `MOVE_FROM_TOP`, `MOVE_FROM_BOTTOM`, `SLIDE_OUT_TO_LEFT`, `SLIDE_OUT_TO_RIGHT`, `SLIDE_OUT_TO_TOP`, `SLIDE_OUT_TO_BOTTOM`, `MOVE_OUT_TO_LEFT`, `MOVE_OUT_TO_RIGHT`, `MOVE_OUT_TO_TOP`, `MOVE_OUT_TO_BOTTOM`, `SMART_ANIMATE`. Components MUST preserve every token and supply its working native transition behavior through existing compositing/animation owners; unknown or not-yet-supported mapping is explicit and is not accepted as feature parity. The MT carries the complete list and tests its affected distinct direction/entry/exit semantics rather than treating similar names as aliases; `NONE` creates no invented source duration default.

**[STU-PRO-173] Closed slide-transition curve vocabulary and explicit mapping.** The source record's `curve` is exactly `EASE_IN`, `EASE_OUT`, `EASE_IN_AND_OUT`, `LINEAR`, `GENTLE`, `QUICK`, `BOUNCY`, `SLOW`. These source names MUST remain distinct from [STU-PRO-120]'s Studio-declared preset identities. Native evaluation stores the actual four-number Bézier/spring tuple required by [STU-PRO-119]/[STU-PRO-120] while the import projection retains its original source token and version. The captured declaration supplies no numeric tuple, and similarly named Studio presets do not prove source equivalence. The affected MT's FIRST acceptance criterion MUST pin the numeric mapping or original-produced curve/appearance oracle and its tolerance before accepting faithful source rendering. Until then, preserve the source token with an explicit unavailable or approved approximation/loss outcome; do not silently claim identical easing. `Hold` remains timeline-only and is not added to this eight-token union.

**[STU-PRO-174] Slide timing folded into Pulse.** The source `timing` record has required `type` exactly `ON_CLICK` or `AFTER_DELAY`, and optional `delay: number` explicitly in seconds. Raw source absence and zero are different and MUST round-trip distinctly. Any source runtime normalization that ignores/resets delay for `ON_CLICK` is separate from the preserved raw projection and must cite its profile; an example value is not a default. Pulse converts source duration/delay into the existing integer 254 016 000 000-ticks-per-second time base using checked range/conversion and explicit rounding/loss metadata, retains raw seconds and provenance, and never inherits prototype-millisecond bounds. Native playback/manual advance, skipped-slide traversal, timer cancellation and deterministic ordering reuse the existing presentation/interaction scheduler and bounded admission path; realtime callbacks must not perform blocking diagnostics or database work. Shared Controls, typed commands, Argus snapshots and both manual layers expose authored timing, effective timing and cancellation outcomes. No feature implementation is accepted until its affected timing and overflow cases are proven.
